messages.author: 6eec351ad1d5a711
messages.subject: warnings analysing censored CMR data
parts:
Morning all,

I am analysing some simulated CMR data which has a combination of interval censored and right censored data but I am consistently getting a host of warnings when I run the model.

This a slightly simplified version of the model that I am running...

tKD - is a vector of recovered dead times (NA if never recovered)
tL - is the last observed alive time
tD - is a vector of unknown death times

## define censoring matrices
cint <- cbind(tL, tKD)
cint[is.na(tKD), 2] <- cint[is.na(tKD), 1]
cint[is.na(tKD), 1] <- 0
censored <- ifelse(!is.na(tKD), 1, 2)
censored[1:5]<-NA
tD <- rep(NA, length(tKD))
dind <- rep(1, length(tKD))


CMR.code <- nimbleCode({
  
  ## survival components for dead individuals
  for (i in 1:nind) {
    
    ## likelihood for interval-truncated exponential
    censored[i] ~ dinterval(tD[i], cint[i, ])
    tD[i] ~ dexp(a)
    
    ## sampling component
    pd[i] <- exp(y[i] * log(mean.p) + (min(floor(tD[i]), tM[i]) - y[i]) * log(1 - mean.p))
    dind[i] ~ dbern(pd[i])
  }
  
  ## priors
  a ~ dexp(1)
  mean.p ~ dunif(0, 1)
  
})

## set up other components of model
CMR.Consts <- list(nind = nind, tM = tM)
CMR.data <- list(y = y, cint = cint, censored = censored, tD = tD, dind = dind)
CMR.inits <- list(
  tD = apply(cint, 1, function(x) runif(1, x[1], x[2])),
  a = 0.1, 
  mean.p = runif(1,0,1)
)

But when I run the model I consistently receive the below warnings for the right censored individuals, despite the model running?
warning: logProb of data node censored[1]: logProb is -Inf.
warning: logProb of data node dind[1]: logProb is NA or NaN.

Additonally mean.p seems to be constrained below 0.5 when it shouldnt be?!

Just wondering if anyone can see any errors in the code that I have missed?

Many thanks,

Dave

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: warnings analysing censored CMR data
parts:
Hi Dave, a couple things to get you started, and if needed we can then iterate:

1) the warning about the logProb of dind[1] is presumably because
pd[1] is NA or NaN or because pd[1] is outside the (0,1) interval.
Please take a look at model$pd and then try to see what the
computation of "pd[i] <- ...." is doing in terms of what inputs lead
to that situation for pd[1].

2) The warning about logProb of censored[1] is probably because the
input value you provide for censored[1] is not inside the correct
interval given the current values of the arguments for dinterval(),
namely td[1] and cint[1,]. Please check all those values and make sure
you are providing initial values that are all consistent with each
other.

-chris

messages.subject: Re: warnings analysing censored CMR data
parts:
Hi Chris,

Thanks for th info, yes... having sent the initial email over I went back through and yes... all to do with the initial values!  So thank you!  I now have set up a function that creates an initial value dependent on whether it it interval or right censored, and the warnings have disappeared!

Many thanks for getting back to me, much appreciated.

Dave
